title: Observability Unification, LLM Quality, and Operator Autonomy Roadmap
author: Evan Chen
content:
Overview

This roadmap lays out a 15-month program to unify observability signals, introduce automated LLM quality regression detection, and deliver operator autonomy features that reduce time-to-restore and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for platform incidents. The work focuses on three coordinated pillars:

1) Observability Unification: single telemetry schema, cross-system SLI synthesis, unified trace/span conventions.
2) LLM Quality Monitoring: prompt set-driven regression detection, sample-based semantic diffs, and auto-alerting.
3) Operator Autonomy: safe operator actions, runbook automation, and decision-support UIs.

Goals and guiding principles

- Deliver a single observability contract for platform components by Q2 2027.
- Detect >95% of production LLM quality regressions in top-50 tenants within 30 minutes of occurrence.
- Reduce manual operator interventions for common degradations by 40% within 12 months of rollout.
- Preserve cost visibility and avoid telemetry bloat: new signals must pass a cost/benefit gate.

Success metrics (how we will measure progress)

- Observability coverage: percent of services emitting required fields in the unified schema (target 90% by Q2 2027).
- Regression detection recall/precision on historical labeled regressions (target recall 0.95, precision 0.85).
- Operator effort reduction: median number of manual steps per incident for top-10 runbooks (target -40%).
- SLO compliance: maintain platform token-generation 99.9% availability across regions during migrations.

Timeline and high-level milestones (quarterly)

| Quarter | Milestone | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Q4 2026 | Program kickoff, schema draft, gating policy | Data + Observability Eng | Schema v0.1 published, gating checklist approved |
| Q1 2027 | Core signal producers adapted (runtime, allocator, kv-cache) | Runtime, Eng-Platform | 50% of services reporting schema fields; sample dashboards|
| Q2 2027 | Cross-SLI synthesis and alerting framework v1 | Observability | SLI joiner service running in staging; first cross-SLI alert generated|
| Q3 2027 | LLM quality eval pipeline (prompt-set hooks + diffs) pilot | Applied ML + Monitoring | Pilot on 10 tenants; automated regression alerts fired and triaged|
| Q4 2027 | Operator autonomy v1: safe-mode runbook automation | Eng-Platform + SRE | 3 runbooks automated with canary and operator override; post-deployment drill completed|
| Q1 2028 | Platform-wide rollout and retrospective | Product + Eng | 90% schema coverage; regression recall/precision goals met; rollout retro published|

Workstreams and owners

- Telemetry Schema and Contract (Owner: Data Observability)
  - Deliverables: schema v1, egress/cost guidelines, migration kit
  - Key fields: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, input_token_count, output_token_count, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, route_policy

- Cross-SLI Synthesis Engine (Owner: Eng-Platform Observability)
  - Deliverables: SLI joiner service, SLO composer, dashboard templates, alert enrichment pipeline
  - Runtime must support tokenized SLIs (token-cost SLO) and quality-linked SLIs (semantic-fidelity-score)

- LLM Quality Monitoring (Owner: Applied ML + Monitoring)
  - Deliverables: prompt-set manager, ground-truth corpus, semantic-diff model, regression scoring service, labeled-regression dataset
  - Integration points: sampling hooks at inference gateway, synthetic prompt injection for coverage, periodic offline evals

- Operator Autonomy & Runbook Automation (Owner: SRE + Eng-Platform)
  - Deliverables: operator action catalog, safe-mode DSL, automation runner, operator UI with decision playback and rollback buttons
  - Safety primitives: action dry-run, canary scope, feature flag gating, auditable operator approvals

- Dashboard and Alert Migration (Owner: Observability UX)
  - Deliverables: dashboard library, alert-rule translation tool, alert prioritization matrix, oncall training curriculum

Detailed rollout plan: dashboards and alerts

1) Audit & baseline (2 weeks): inventory current dashboards and rules. Produce baseline metrics: duplicate alerts, alert-noise rate, mean time to ack (MTTA).
2) Rule consolidation (4 weeks): map existing rules to the schema and de-duplicate. Apply priority tags: sev0, sev1, sev2.
3) Enrichment and context (6 weeks): wire SLI joiner to include relevant spans and model variant metadata in alert payloads.
4) Phased enablement (rolling 2-week windows): enable new rules for 10% of teams, collect operator feedback, tune thresholds.
5) Global switch (planned maintenance): flip new rules as primary, keep old rules in failover for 30 days.

Example alert rule (Prometheus-style) and enrichment guidance

```
# Alert: cross-tenant-token-latency-spike
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id)) > 1500
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: "sev1"
annotations:
  summary: "P95 token latency > 1500ms for {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-operator-resumption-after-region-split-and-traffic-reconverge-2026"
  extra_context: "model_variant={{ $labels.model_variant }}, route_policy={{ $labels.route_policy }}"
```

Enrichment: alerts MUST include tenant_id, model_variant, route_policy, and a top-5 correlated signals block (recent token-burst, kv_cache_hit-rate delta, alloc_evictions).

Migration checklist (service owners)

1. Ensure service emits the unified schema fields. Use the migration kit to validate spans and metrics.
2. Add one sample synthetic prompt to the sampling pipeline (for LLM quality coverage).
3. Enable canary telemetry ingestion in staging; verify dashboards render expected values.
4. Participate in a runbook rehearsal (operator can trigger the automation and observe safe rollback).
5. File a post-migration verification ticket with screenshots and SLI delta comparisons.

Operator autonomy: safety story and allowed actions

- Allowed automated actions (with canary and operator approval):
  - tenant soft-throttle and burst-credit drain
  - model-variant swap to pre-approved fallback (quantized/warm variant)
  - emergency re-route to regional standby (read-only operator consent required)
- Not allowed as automation: schema-change rollbacks, billing-affecting quota resets, long-lived capacity reservation changes

Operator UI expectations

- One-click context bundle: includes correlated traces, recent synthetic prompts and their outputs, token cost delta, recent eval score trend.
- Decision playback: preview of what a model-swap would do (sample inputs routed through fallback variant)
- Audit trail: who triggered what, commands, approvals, and automatic revert timers

Risk register and mitigations

- Risk: telemetry volume growth causing storage/cost blowout.
  - Mitigation: data retention tiers, enforced sampling rates, and a telemetry-cost approval step for new signals.
- Risk: false positive quality alerts causing unnecessary rollbacks.
  - Mitigation: require 2-signal correlation (semantic-diff + user-facing metric drop) before auto-action; operator approval default for first 3 months.
- Risk: operator mistrust due to opaque automation.
  - Mitigation: decision playback, dry-run mode, and post-action explanations surfaced in UI.

Dependencies and cross-team coordination

- Applied ML: provide semantic diff model and labeled regression artifacts.
- Runtime team: emit KV cache and batching signals and support a sampling hook.
- Billing team: expose token cost attribution API for SLO cost-aware dashboards.
- SRE/content: update runbooks to use new field names and decision points.

Acceptance criteria for program completion

- 90% of core platform services emit required schema fields in prod.
- Regression detection pilot demonstrates target recall/precision on a held-out set and live incidents.
- 3 critical runbooks automated with operator override and audited rollbacks.
- Oncall MTTA reduced by 20% and MTTM reduced by 30% for top-10 incident classes linked to LLM regressions.

Retro plan and continuous improvement

- Post-rollout retrospective at 30/90/180 days with cross-team stakeholders. Agenda: telemetry cost vs. signal value, false positive analysis, operator feedback, SLO drift.
- Quarterly evaluation of semantic diff models using new labeled examples curated from customer escalations.

Open questions for leadership and design review

- What threshold of telemetry-level cost increase is acceptable for new signals (proposal: 5% of observability budget per quarter cap)?
- Policy decision: should we permit automatic model-variant swap without operator approval after 6 months of high confidence?
- Runbook ownership: who signs off on the final automation playbooks for customers in Dedicated (suggestion: Eng-Platform + Customer Success joint ownership)?

Appendices

A. Minimal unified telemetry schema (excerpt)
| field | type | description | required |
|---|---|---|---:|
| request_id | string | per-request unique id | yes |
| tenant_id | string | customer tenancy id | yes |
| model_variant | string | model version + quantization tag | yes |
| input_tokens | int | tokenized input length | yes |
| output_tokens | int | tokenized output length | yes |
| latency_ms | histogram | request latency distribution | yes |
| kv_cache_hit | float | kv cache hit rate | no |
| batch_size | int | observed batch size | no |

C. Example playbook snippet (operator-facing)
1) Confirm alert details and cross-signal correlation.
2) Open decision playback UI and run sample through fallback variant.
3) If fallback output is acceptable, authorize model swap for a 15-minute canary window.
4) Monitor semantic diff score and user-facing latency. If metrics return to baseline, promote change; otherwise revert and file postmortem.
